Question: What is wisdom? How do you gain wisdom?
Answer: Wisdom is the ability of foresight. It‘s making the right decision even when it’s hard and doesn’t immediately benefit you because through reference experience, introspection and mistakes, you‘ve learned and discovered for yourself which decisions create win-win situations in the long run and which decisions lead to horrible outcomes. You gain it by learning from past mistakes and from the mistakes of others. But in order to do so, we need humility and to be open-minded enough to think and feel beyond ourselves (our pride and ego). Many people struggle with this, which is why there is a shortage of wise people in modern society and why modern dating is as chaotic and dysfunctional as it is today. I.e. in the context of dating and relationships, a wise decision would be to not get into a relationship with someone who‘s either married or not over their ex even if you feel insanely attracted to them, because through foresight or observing the mistakes of others you just know that this wont end well for you.

Question: How do I stop myself from thinking about my ex?
Answer: Intrusive and seemingly uncontrollable thought-loops of an ex is something that most people struggle with even many years after the breakup. And the thing about this is that you can’t ever turn these memories off like a lightswitch. Because if it were that easy, nobody would have this problem. So, that’s why you need to accept that these thoughts and memories will most likely be there your whole life. It’s just that the more you heal, let go, improve yourself and rediscover life without them, the shorter these thoughts become, the easier it gets to snap out of useless and endless rumination/obsession and the less intense these memories and thoughts become. Here’s how to do that: Go no contact Especially if right now you’re in an open-ended, unclear and complicated situationship with your ex where they become increasingly more avoidant or manipulative or where you’re constantly left doubting yourself and obsess over trying to decipher the meaning behind all of their behaviors. Otherwise you’re not allowing yourself to heal and improve. If you don’t go no contact (as in you keep accepting being treated like an option or doormat), you’ll remain stuck in this pattern where you heal a bit but eventually get re-traumatized, undo the healing or re-open certain emotional wounds because your ex keeps coming back into your life to fuck shit up. The only way to break out of this pattern for real and start healing for good without constantly getting re-traumatized like this is to put your own well-being first and be firm with the no contact boundary. To put an end to being led on, manipulated or used. If you’re on relatively good terms, you don’t need to be mean about it. Just letting them know that you really need this space and distance to improve yourself and to heal is enough. Whether your ex likes that or not is irrelevant. Because you’re no longer in a relationship and you have to put yourself first if your intention is to heal and improve. This is a very mature, grounded and rational response to such situations. They have to respect this and deal with the fact that you do not accept their behaviors or offers for friendship anymore. They have to accept that they can no longer have their cake and eat it too. Important sidenote: if you have kids together, choose low contact over full no contact. This means keeping interactions with your ex at an absolute minimum, to only reach out to or respond to them to handle the kids stuff. If possible, try to create a set schedule with your ex for the days where you get the kids and the days where they they get them. Also, don’t use your kids as an excuse to gain access to your ex. Don’t constantly ask them if they have time to talk or something like that. Keep your interactions as minimal as possible and only reach out when it’s something important that has to do with the kids. Because your ex is going to feel the shift in your energy and personality either way as long as you work on yourself. Improve your mindset You can’t always control your thoughts but you can be aware of the nature and direction of them and change it from there. I.e. when you catch yourself slipping back into endless rumination, put your foot down and decide to no longer go down this path, because so far it has only made things worse for yourself. Therefore, intentionally put your focus elsewhere, to something that helps you heal or get ahead in life. Because to a large degree, the quality of our mindset dictates the quality of our life, well-being, success and personal growth. Make sure that your mind is working for you, not against you. Follow the 1% rule The 1% rule is a simple yet very powerful habit that helps you focus on growth, to improve yourself and rebuild self-confidence. All you need to do is to reflect on your day before going to bed and ask yourself: ‘Am I smarter/more aware/better than yesterday?’ If for you the answer is that you only got 1% better/more aware/smarter than yesterday, then that’s still a win and it means that you have won, that you have done the right thing and are on the right track. Do this every single day before going to bed and you’ll be 365% better by the next year.

Question: Do dumpers ever feel remorse even if s/he in a relationship right a month after the breakup?
Answer: It depends on a few nuances. Generally though, most dumpers don’t regret it at all and even feel justified in their decision. Because of this, right after the breakup they’re usually so cold, careless and detached and it’s why no amount of begging, pleading, negotiating or chasing works. It‘s because they‘ve already moved on and are fixated on never being with their dumpee again. At least not for the first couple of months post-breakup and especially not if they jumped straight into a rebound relationship. That’s why many times, the pain catches up with the dumper at a later point but, only if they rushed their decision to breakup. If it wasn’t rushed and they thought the decision to leave through well, then they will be gone for good. In which case the only choice you as the dumpee really have is to gracefully accept that it’s over, move on, go no contact and never reach out to them again as a way to keep your dignity, sanity and self-respect in tact. If it was rushed, then the pain eventually catches up with them as soon as the dumpee heals, lets go, moves on and changes in positive ways, when they discover that their rebound wasn’t as good as the dumpee after all or when the dumper really feels the absence of the dumpee in their life. It’s only then when they start reflecting on their decision.
